endorsements.quote: Patients must be notified that they are interacting with an automated machine.
Autonomy: Any patient interaction with an AI chatbot must be consensual.
One potential implication of AI chatbots in this domain is whether patients will be able to make the decision to “opt out” of interacting with these tools.

unlisted_practices: Do not use AI chatbots as substitutes for the physician-patient relationship.
Prohibit plastic surgery patients from using AI chatbots for information gathering, patient education, or medical advice in their current form.
Have a clinician review and approve any AI-generated content, such as note templates and discharge instructions, before deployment in a clinical setting.
Have clinical staff review all patient interactions with an AI chatbot to ensure accurate and unbiased conversation.
Safeguard patient information shared with chatbots against unauthorized access or disclosure and ensure HIPAA compliance.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective article examining the technical capabilities, limitations, and ethical implications (autonomy, nonmaleficence, beneficence, justice) of ChatGPT in plastic surgery clinical practice, recommending cautious use and guideline development.
